qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

In the Geraneia Mountains, which comprise Natura 2000 areas and a wildlife reserve, plans to install 57 wind turbines that are up to 180 metres high, accompanied by electrochemical energy storage plants, have been put to public consultation. According to the studies carried out, the project involves extensive excavations, including new road excavations, large quantities of concrete and extensive cabling networks. In addition, part of the works are to take place in areas already affected by major wildfires in recent years. The area also hosts important protected fauna species and is a flyway of European importance. Meanwhile, local communities as well as the regional councils of Attica and the Peloponnese have voiced their objections. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: Does it intend to examine whether special measures are needed to protect recently burnt Natura 2000 areas before authorisation is given for new extensive technical works to go ahead?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.10.2026) Ori Geraneia is a special area of conservation (SAC) designated under the Habitats Directive1 (Site code GR2530005)2. Article 6(2) of the Habitats Directive requires Member States to take appropriate steps to prevent the deterioration of habitats, including from foreseeable natural disasters such as fires3 and if appropriate, to bring the negative impact to an end by stopping the activity and, if necessary, by taking restoration measures. In accordance with Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive, the Greek competent authorities need to ensure that plans and projects, including wind farms, do not adversely affect the integrity of Natura 2000 sites, either individually or in combination with other plans or projects. The assessment of the project’s implications for the site must take into account the site’s conservation objectives, as well as the current status of protected species and habitats, including post-fire impacts. The Commission has issued guidance on the application of these provisions4, on wind energy and EU nature legislation5 and on Natura 2000 and climate change6, where post-fire recovery is mentioned. In addition, the Nature Restoration Regulation7 requires Member States to put in place measures to restore degraded forest habitats and to enhance biodiversity of forest ecosystems. Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, it is primarily the responsibility of the Greek authorities to ensure that wind farm projects are developed in full compliance with EU environmental legislation.
